newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak blue chips close mostly down, SAX dips.
newsitem.headline: Slovak blue chips close mostly down, SAX dips.

text.p: Leading Slovak shares closed mostly lower in light trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Wednesday, as the market awaits a key parliamentary vote on a controversial securities bill, dealers said.
"There is little movement (in the market) because both buyers and sellers are waiting to see if parliament passes the law which will create a great deal of uncertainty," said Jozef Cimra of ING bank.
One of the most controversial clauses of the new bill allows the majority stockholder of a company to arbitrarily suspend trading of its shares on the stock market.
Oil refiner Slovnaft shed 20 crowns to close at 730 and VUB bank also closed down 20 crowns at 1,680. Steelmaker VSZ gained one crown to close at 500 on a volume of 2,800 shares.
"There is no big movement in VSZ and it appears that investors appear satisfied with its current level," Cimra said. "But we may see a slight upward movement next week."

Trading in gas and oil storage company Nafta was suspended on Wednesday due to a general shareholders' meting at which the firm's new owners announced an ambitious one billion investment plan for the next eight year period.
Analysts said the move had done little to shore up the firm's sagging image and Cimra said he saw Nafta's share price slipping further from its present 1,373 crown level.
"I see no good prospects for Nafta because the investment plan lacked specifics," Cimra said.
Overall volume fell to 249,690 shares from 564,681 stocks traded on Tuesday. Turnover shrunk to 69.44 million crowns from 324.83 million crowns on Tuesday.
